title: China Stockpiled Oil, and Now It Could Dominate the Energy Landscape
partialText: The war with Iran revealed just how much influence the world’s biggest oil importer has over prices and other countries’ supplies of jet fuel, gasoline and diesel.

title: Global Economy Is Running Out of Wiggle Room
partialText: Many countries blunted the most painful effects of the energy shock from the war in Iran. But prices remain elevated and risks are multiplying.

title: Who Will Win the Midterms? Republicans Are Reeling.
partialText: The party is putting up a costly defense of states and districts that President Trump won easily in 2024. And in places like Georgia, strategists wonder if it’s too late.

title: G.O.P. Representative Breaks With Trump in Ad: Hispanics ‘Feel Betrayed’
partialText: Representative María Elvira Salazar, a three-term representative from Miami, won re-election by 20 percentage points in 2024. Her ad suggests worry among some Republicans about their standing with Hispanic voters.

title: Can a Republican Become Governor of New York? Blakeman Makes His Case.
partialText: Bruce Blakeman is trying to unseat Gov. Kathy Hochul, a Democrat, attacking her on the economy, crime and immigration by using Trump-like tactics and A.I.

title: OpenAI Discloses Six New Incidents of ‘Concerning' A.I. Behavior
partialText: The artificial intelligence company also released a framework for reporting when its systems go wrong.

title: Why Is It So Difficult To Regulate A.I.?
partialText: There has been considerable debate over regulating the artificial intelligence industry, but much of that effort has stalled. Cecilia Kang, a technology reporter for The New York Times, explains why.

title: What Happens When A.I. Stops Doing What Humans Want?
partialText: “Alignment” is the science of teaching A.I. to do what is in line with human preferences, ethics and judgment. But, at times, the systems have gone rogue.

title: A.I. Agents as ‘Co-Scientists’? This Lab Says They Could Speed Drug Research.
partialText: A.I. is already a powerful tool for scientific discovery. Now, some biomedical researchers are teaching it to do even more.

title: Fed Chairman Warsh Escapes Trump’s Ire Over Interest Rate Increase
partialText: The president blasted the rest of the Fed — and kept up his demand for a cut — but spared Fed Chairman Kevin M. Warsh from the criticism.

title: Are Trump’s Official Papers His Personal Property?
partialText: The administration argues that presidential papers are like those of Supreme Court justices.

title: The Face of London in the 1960s Is Living Her Best Life
partialText: The face of London in the 1960s is living her best life at the age of 77.

title: Trump Air Force One Photos Fuel Kennedy Center Demolition Speculation
partialText: Images captured through the windows of Air Force One showed President Trump reviewing a poster with the title “Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED.”

title: Judge Allows Kennedy Center to Remain Temporarily Closed
partialText: The federal judge denied a Democratic lawmaker’s request for an emergency hearing on the closure, which began on Tuesday.

title: U.S. Strike on Iranian School May Have Been War Crime, U.N. Report Says
partialText: Mistakes that led to the deaths of more than a hundred children “went beyond negligence,” investigators said. They also cited a separate strike the same day that killed a reported 22 civilians.

title: Russia and China Veto U.S. Bid to Renew U.N. Monitoring of Iran Nuclear Program
partialText: The conflict underscored the distance between world powers over the United States’ pressure campaign on Iran.

title: Major Iranian Airline Suspends Several Flights Abroad, Adding to Isolation
partialText: The carrier, Mahan Air, said it would stop flying to neighboring countries just over a week after the United States imposed sweeping sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry.

title: To a Binational Tribe, Trump’s Border Wall Feels Like Betrayal
partialText: An escalating confrontation on Native land southwest of Tucson threatens to upend decades of uneasy cooperation between the Tohono O’odham Nation and the United States.

title: C.J. Huff Rebuilt His City’s Devastated Schools. Then Came the Backlash.
partialText: One superintendent is trying to apply what he’s learned to other shattered districts — and reckoning with the toll of the disaster on his own life.

title: The Next Gene-Editing Technology May Also Be the Oldest
partialText: Scientists have discovered a powerful gene-targeting system in viruses. Billions of years old, VIPR seems to predate CRISPR and may be even more powerful.

title: This Rare Gene Drastically Raises Lung Cancer Risk in People Who Never Smoked
partialText: The gene is found predominantly in Southern Appalachia and may be one of the most powerful cancer-risk mutations ever found.

title: Gustavo Dudamel’s New York Era Has Begun. Try to Keep Up.
partialText: The New York Philharmonic’s season started with a barnstorming tour of Manhattan to celebrate Dudamel’s arrival as music and artistic director.

title: Watching Bigots Erupt
partialText: This is what I see when I look at the picture Bo French hates.

title: The $15,000 Settlement That Destroyed My Father’s Life
partialText: A 35-foot fall didn’t kill Michael Wagner. The nearly 18-year failure of the safety net did. Before he died, he recorded 694 videos explaining how.
